title: Persisted style objects must never carry runtime-owned fields like visible
trigger: A transient UI state (subtitle hidden by a study mode, user toggle) is silently reverted whenever ANY settings write lands, because saveSettings read-modify-write drags the full style objects into changes.settings.newValue and the listener rebuilds visible from a stale flag.
principle: Split ownership at the choke point: persisted styles carry appearance only; runtime fields (visible, heldCue, playing) are engine-owned. Three rules: (1) on storage.onChanged merge persisted fields over the engine's current runtime fields, never the reverse; (2) strip runtime fields before persisting (const { visible: _v, ...persisted } = style); (3) guard the engine's updateSettings choke point so even a missed writer can't re-assert visibility while a mode owns it. Fixing individual writers is whack-a-mole — every future saveSettings caller would reintroduce the stomp.

cases.context: Listen-Check hid subtitles, then a delayed persistFieldMapping save ~500ms after the mode click carried stored visible:true through onStorageChanged and re-showed subtitles mid blind-listen.

applyFor: Any field owned by a state machine but persisted in a style blob
